# Arcane fixture harness preflight — 2026-10-13

Offline verification passed **30 deterministic checks**. The new synthetic JSONL protocol double forwards the declared fixture_action callback to the copied in-memory fixture and returns its result to the requesting peer. Missing/disabled execution capability, registration without a callback, scope mismatch, duplicates and broad access all fail closed. **No native CLI, inference, discovery or paid dispatch occurred.**

The eight-turn authorization remains consumed/sealed. Its failed evaluation, 0/4 task passes in each variant and no-guide-approval conclusion remain intact. No frozen production source, test or script was changed.

## What the evidence establishes

The frozen disabled feature list contains code_mode_host (frozen/harness/preflight.mjs:15). The thread declaration contains exactly one function tool, fixture_action, with operations read, commit_source, reconcile and apply_asset. All eight saved outputs have zero callback receipts and zero fixture traces. Final responses report unavailable execution; those are model-reported errors, not native executor attestations.

The old readiness check established exact model/effort, sandbox/settings, disabled inherited MCP servers and disabled skills. It did not establish dynamic-tool execution capability or observe a fixture request/result round-trip. Registration was therefore treated as executable readiness without evidence. That missing guard is the precise demonstrated harness defect.

Saved InitializeResponse exposes userAgent, codexHome and platform fields. The saved modelProvider capabilities response exposes only imageGeneration and webSearch. ThreadStartResponse does not attest fixture execution. The saved feature list identifies code_mode_host as a known flag, but does not prove the model-to-host routing dependency. No native internal error receipt, effective executor tool inventory or capability attestation was retained.

**The internal native reason for zero callbacks is not precisely provable from these records.** Disabling code_mode_host is consistent with the responses, but enabling it alone is not a verified fix. The earlier causal wording was stronger than the evidence supports; this new diagnosis qualifies it without editing any sealed artifact.

## Corrected offline contract

fixture-policy.json binds the exact declared tool hash, model/effort, fixture-only route and disabled shell, arbitrary commands, filesystem, external data, network, apps/plugins, multi-agent, Studio and uploads. Synthetic execution evidence is bound to that policy and declaration. It is explicitly labeled synthetic and is supplied through a host-code seam, not an invented native RPC field.

The gate validates the required execution capability before synthetic setup, then registers dynamicTools through a synthetic thread/start exchange. A separate synthetic server-originated item/tool/call read is serialized as JSONL, validated and forwarded to the fixture. Its response is serialized back, matched to the request and checked for disposable fixture scope. Only that observed round-trip passes local preflight. An advertised capability or declaration acknowledgment without a callback fails.

The router prebinds thread and synthetic challenge/turn identity. It rejects other namespaces/tools, unknown operations, malformed/oversized frames, incorrect argument types, irrelevant fields, duplicate request/call IDs and a ninth fixture call. Its only executor is fixture.call; it contains no shell, general code executor, network, process launcher or credential access. Error responses preserve success:false for a fixture CAS conflict. Positive checks exercise the concurrent manual-edit race and exact unknown-asset reconciliation entirely in memory.

There is no paid dispatch or unseal implementation. turn/start is permanently rejected by the synthetic peer; unknown methods are rejected. A successful synthetic result always has nativeEvaluationEligible:false. This proves the offline forwarding contract, not native runtime availability, model behavior or skill effectiveness.

## Exact changes proposed for a later authorized evaluation

1. Build a new evaluation directory and new authorization ledger. Do not change or reuse the old claim, seal, results or harness.
2. At the frozen feature-list equivalent (frozen/harness/preflight.mjs:15), make code_mode_host a separately verified required execution capability. Candidate configuration: remove it from unconditional disabled[] and set features.code_mode_host=true only after native evidence establishes a fixture-only route. Keep code_mode=false and every existing shell/unified_exec/browser/network/app/plugin/Studio restriction. This candidate is unverified; do not enable broad access to compensate.
3. At the consumed-slot boundary equivalent (frozen/harness/run.mjs:66), require exact policy/tool/model binding plus an observed supported zero-paid native fixture read/result round-trip before any intent consumption or turn/start. Missing, disabled, unknown or unsupported capability/probe evidence stops before paid dispatch.
4. Keep the existing single fixture_action declaration and typed schema. Use the corrected callback validation/deduplication/binding rules from fixture-router.mjs, with a separate disposable preflight binding. Do not adopt an unknown first callback turn ID.
5. Retain the single-use cap, fsynced consumed intent, no retry/replacement policy, ephemeral state and separate baseline/assisted grading. Offline preflight success cannot satisfy native execution or guide approval gates.

**Remaining native prerequisite:** the saved protocol provides no attested execution-capability or supported zero-paid callback-probe interface. Synthetic executionEvidence()/probeRead() are local test seams, not native methods. A later adapter needs authoritative native capability evidence and a supported uncharged probe route. If that route is unavailable, stop; do not silently use a paid turn as preflight or treat this synthetic success as authorization.

- diagnosis.json separates proven omissions, model-reported failure and unproven native causality.
- later-evaluation-changes.json contains proposal-only source/config changes and the native prerequisite.
